searchText: I'm a little unclear on the format of the `access_list` in 2930, is it supposed to be in RLP format (e.g.`rlp([[addr1,[key1a,key1b]],[addr2,[key2a]]])`) or just the data binary packed together (`addr1 || key1a || key2a || addr2 || key2a`)? My assumption has been RLP encoded but I don't see that fully spelled out. I'm happy to provide a PR clarifying either way once I'm sure which it should be. The first. Awesome I'll try to come up with a PR with wording that makes that more obvious. Actually one more question: the overall `access_list` can be empty, but can the list of storage keys? That is to say, is `rlp([[addr1, [] ]])` a valid storage list? If not I think the grammar needs to be further clarified since the "zero or more" implies an empty list is acceptable. Sure since you don't need any storage slots if you just need to update the balance of an account. oh wait the example actually shows the 2nd one as empty 🙂 ok cool, got it! The fact that the lists can be empty kind of forces RLP encoding vs binary packing, since the binary packed format could be ambiguous. Hopefully last question: for EIP-2930/1559, would one expect the `v` field in the JSON response for say `eth_getTransactionByHash` to be of the form `0x0|0x1` or continue to be in the EIP-155 `chainId * 2 + 35 + y` format? My vote/inclination is for 0x0 or 0x1, but am also a little unclear on the history of why it was `27 + 0|1` before EIP-155. <@!388751025789468672> yeah should be 0x0 or 0x1 -- 27 comes some ECC in old implementations (https://bitcoin.stackexchange.com/questions/83035/how-to-determine-first-byte-recovery-id-for-signatures-message-signing) for `v` we have both `v` and `standardV` field even for legacy transaction
